title: The Nawab Torments Subeg Singh’s Son before His Father

blocks.text: Unable to move Subeg Singh directly, the nawab has Subeg Singh's young son tortured and hung up before his father's eyes. The violence is calculated to turn paternal grief into religious surrender, making the child a lever in the attempt to break the elder Singh's resolve.

Instead, Subeg Singh blesses the child's firmness and reads the boy's suffering as honorable rather than shameful. The page turns what should have been emotional blackmail into another witness to Sikh steadfastness, with father and son reinforcing one another under terror.

The nawab then shifts from spectacle to temptation, offering life, estate, protection, and future status if either of them will accept Islam. Torture and reward become two faces of the same coercive project, but neither is yet enough to compel consent.
